name: Client Hint: form factors
plain: Device class list: Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, XR, Automotive, EInk, Watch.
meaning: Newer replacement for guessing from the mobile flag and screen size. Lets a site serve car, e-reader, VR or tablet layouts. Some users report more than one factor.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: formFactors
fields.range: Automotive, Desktop, EInk, Mobile, Tablet, Watch, XR (combinable)

limits.headline: Can tell if you use a desktop, phone, tablet, watch, or car screen
limits.user_action: Nothing. The site asks and Chromium answers without a prompt
can: See device types such as Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, Watch, XR, or Automotive
Show a layout that fits an e-reader, car, or headset
Fit the page to your device without guessing from screen size
Learn about more than one type if your device reports it
cannot: Work in Firefox, Safari, or on iPhone
Get an answer until the site asks for it
Be sure; some devices report oddly
limits.reach_label: Device type, only when the site asks
limits.differs: Chromium browsers answer. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: Tells a site what kind of device you use: desktop, phone, tablet, headset, car, e-reader or watch.

marketing.name: User-Agent Client Hints
marketing.pitch: Chrome offers sites a standard way to ask about the device when they need it.

story.for_you: You never see the question. What you see is a page that fits your device: a big touch layout on a car screen, or a simpler page on an e-reader. It helps pages look right without guessing from screen size.
story.for_makers: The old method guessed from screen size and a mobile flag. A direct list of device types lets sites serve the right layout and the right controls. Some devices report more than one type, which also makes a handy signal.

use_cases.example: A web app in a car's browser shows large buttons and voice prompts instead of tiny links.
A WebXR site detects a headset and offers its 3D room instead of a flat page.
A browser game offers touch buttons on tablets and keyboard hints on desktops.
A streaming site serves a simple high-contrast layout to an e-ink reader with no video.
A web shop shows tablet layouts with bigger product photos and fewer columns.
A news site offers a text-first page on slow e-readers.

risks: Multiple answers give a more unique ID

technical_bounds: High entropy, so must be requested
